bugs.title: Pi custom message payload is dropped during normalization
bugs.description: `packages/web/server/lib/pi/bridge-schema.js:278` only preserves `details` for `role === 'custom'` messages and never reads an upstream `payload` field. The translated part then backfills `metadata.pi.payload` from `details` in `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:610`, so any custom payload that differs from `details` is lost before it reaches storage/rendering. This breaks the task goal of preserving custom message `payload` metadata for Web display and plugin interoperability.

bugs.title: Pi confirm/select questions accept invalid freeform answers
bugs.description: Pi `select` and `confirm` requests are mapped onto the generic `QuestionCard` without any constraint metadata in `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:720` and `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:739`. `packages/ui/src/components/chat/QuestionCard.tsx:324` always renders the `Other…` freeform path, so users can submit arbitrary text for what should be fixed-choice requests. The backend then treats any non-empty confirm answer as approval in `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:1198`, meaning answers like `no` or `cancel` still become `{ confirmed: true }`. This can acknowledge Pi confirmation prompts incorrectly and send invalid values back for `select`.

bugs.title: QuestionCard no longer allows freeform answers for non-Pi questions
bugs.description: `packages/ui/src/components/chat/QuestionCard.tsx` now gates the custom-text path on `question.metadata?.bridgeMethod === 'input'`. Native/OpenCode questions do not populate that metadata, so the existing `Other…` textarea disappears and any question with empty options becomes impossible to answer. This regresses the pre-existing ask-user flow while fixing Pi confirm/select validation.

bugs.title: Pi prompt failure leaves session stuck in busy state
bugs.description: `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:1128` marks the session busy before sending `set_model` / `prompt`, but there is no rollback on command/process startup failure. Reproduced by creating a runtime with a missing `cliPath`: `promptAsync()` rejects and `getSessionStatus()[session.id]` remains `{ type: 'busy' }`, so the UI never recovers from startup/config errors.

bugs.title: Pi SSE bridge drops assistant streaming updates until message end
bugs.description: `handlePiSseStream()` only emits translated events on `message_end`, `tool_execution_end`, and `agent_end`, while `translateOpenCodeMessagesToSseEvents()` only produces full `message.updated` / `message.part.updated` snapshots. The normalized `message_update` assistant stream payloads are never bridged into SSE deltas, so text-only Pi turns do not appear in the Web UI until the whole response finishes. This regresses the existing live-streaming chat behavior for long responses.

bugs.title: Pi prompt bridge strips file attachment content down to a label
bugs.description: `buildPromptTextFromParts()` only serializes file parts as `[file] <path-or-name>` and ignores the attached data URL / payload entirely. In the current Web client, file parts can contain uploaded text or image content, so Pi sessions lose the actual attachment content and only receive a filename placeholder. Prompts that depend on screenshots or uploaded files therefore behave incorrectly under the Pi runtime.

bugs.title: Pi prompt bridge still drops text from server file URL attachments
bugs.description: `buildPromptInputFromParts()` in `packages/web/server/lib/pi/runtime.js:126` only inlines text when the file part carries a data URL or `source.path`. The Web client sends server-backed text attachments and inline `@path` mentions as `type: 'file'`, `mime: 'text/plain'`, `url: 'file:///…'` (see `packages/ui/src/stores/messageStore.ts:646` and `packages/ui/src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx:319`). Repro: calling `buildPromptTextFromParts([{ type: 'file', filename: 'pi-file-url-fixture.txt', mime: 'text/plain', url: 'file:///…' }])` returns `[file] pi-file-url-fixture.txt` instead of embedding the file contents, so Pi still loses the actual attachment text for server files.
